title: Define conversion events and tracking governance
requirements: Identify the primary lead-conversion actions for the site, including booking inquiries, contact submissions, newsletter/subscribe actions, and outbound ticket clicks.
Define a consistent event schema for page views, engagement events, and lead conversions so the same signals can feed Google Tag Manager and Meta Pixel.
Document consent and privacy expectations before firing marketing tags in production.
Establish one source of truth for browser events to avoid double-counting across tags.
notes: DONE (awaiting review). Deliverables: (1) docs/tracking.md — governance contract covering the 6 primary conversion actions, canonical event schema (envelope + catalogue + field conventions), single-source-of-truth architecture, dedupe strategy via event_id, and consent/privacy expectations (Consent Mode v2 default-denied, no PII in dataLayer, PIPEDA/CASL notes). (2) src/lib/tracking.js — SSR-safe, side-effect-free shared module exporting EVENTS, EVENT_CATEGORIES, track(), and typed helpers (trackPageView, trackViewShow, trackTicketClick, trackContact, trackGenerateLead, trackSubscribe); the ONLY entry point for browser events. (3) projects/fever_dream/.env.example — VITE_GTM_CONTAINER_ID, VITE_META_PIXEL_ID, VITE_TRACKING_DEBUG. (4) README.md — new Marketing Tracking & Conversion Governance section. Validation: npx eslint src/lib/tracking.js clean; npm run build (client+SSR+prerender of 16 pages) succeeds. No tags fire in this task by design; downstream tasks implement against this contract.
